title: Harden full-recrawl postflight health retries and failure propagation
source_ref: ops/ledgers/full-recrawl-closeout-2026-07-31.md; tools/recrawl-health.log shows the July 31 run closed green at 09:59:13 PT with api_status=200 api_ok=1 and no lock remains, while the July 30 run recorded completion with api_status=000 api_ok=0. Current tools/recrawl-common.sh finish_wrapper still performs one postflight probe, records completion regardless of api_ok, and returns success. Bounded 10:09 PT proof: health status=ok db=ok, total_sites=4343 avg_score=38, developer=1320, other=850, spam=1.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve the July 31 aggregate closeout and remove the stale active-recrawl boundary; do not start another full recrawl to reproduce the July 30 postflight failure.
Add bounded postflight health retries with logged attempt counts, backoff, final HTTP status, and final api_ok state.
Return nonzero when postflight health remains unhealthy after retries so the installed launchd and sync-state retry path can act.
Run IndexNow only after a healthy postflight and log an explicit skip reason otherwise.
Release the local run lock on success, remote-command failure, postflight failure, interruption, and dry-run paths.
Add fixture tests for immediate success, transient 000 then 200, persistent failure, remote-command failure, exit status, IndexNow gating, and lock release.
Verify the installed recurring path on a later scheduled bounded run records either healthy completion or explicit failed/retry state; do not use a manual broad recrawl as the acceptance test.

acceptance_criteria: Do not register a monitor or use a third-party email while implementing or testing this repair.
Add a pending-confirmation state and one-time confirmation flow; only confirmed rows are eligible for scheduled checks and alerts, while shared-host quarantine remains intact.
Require an explicit consent or inbox-ownership assertion and advertise the email side effect through the MCP tool description and side-effect annotations.

Return stable status and confirmation-delivery fields, avoid exposing an unsubscribe token before confirmation, keep duplicates idempotent, and replace raw internal error propagation with bounded public error classes.

Add tests for missing consent, pending registration, confirmation, expired and replayed tokens, duplicates, delivery failure, legacy active rows, quarantine, rate limits, analytics redaction, token non-disclosure, and REST/MCP parity.

After a later product-worker deploy, verify the MCP schema, confirmation delivery, activation, unsubscribe, redacted analytics, REST parity, and monitor-worker eligibility with a Foundry-owned test inbox.
